card: Validation keeps files queued for pruning in BlockManager across flush retries so they are unlinked after a failed flush recovers. Previously, setFilesToPrune was local to FlushStateToDisk, meaning a flush failure before the block index write would leave pruned blk and rev files on disk until the next node restart. This follows up on review of PR 35714 and is a prerequisite for PR 36738.
evidence: Identified in post-merge review item 7 of PR #35714 by ryanofsky (PR description).
Addresses unhandled failure cases when returning block-file flush errors introduced in #35714 (PR description).
problem: When a flush that prunes block files fails before committing to the block index database (for example, due to disk space check failure or a block file flush error), the set of files to prune is discarded because it is held in a local variable in FlushStateToDisk(). While subsequent flushes commit the pruned state to disk, they do not attempt to delete the physical blk and rev files, leaking disk space until ScanAndUnlinkAlreadyPrunedFiles runs on node restart.

risk.why: A flaw in file tracking or deletion logic could delete block or undo files before they are properly marked pruned on disk or delete active files, causing block data loss.

scope_notes: Three of four commits add unit test coverage for block flush retry failures and pruning test fixture arguments.
summary: Tracks block and undo files queued for pruning across flush attempts in BlockManager rather than discarding them when a flush fails. If a flush fails before writing the block index, any files that were marked as pruned in memory will be deleted on the next successful block index write instead of remaining on disk until the next node restart.
